title: PACE: Geometry-Aware Bridge Transport for Single-Cell Trajectory Inference
abstract: arXiv:2605.18587v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Single-cell trajectory inference from destructive time-course snapshots is fundamentally ill-posed: neither cross-time cell correspondences nor continuous trajectories are observed, so the snapshot distributions alone do not uniquely determine the underlying dynamics. Existing optimal transport and flow-based methods typically couple cells by Euclidean proximity at observed clock times, which can misalign trajectories when development is asynchronous and cells sampled at the same experimental time occupy different latent pseudotime stages. We propose PACE, a trajectory inference framework that recovers geometry-consistent continuous transport dynamics from destructive time-course snapshots through three coupled components. First, PACE constructs a state- and time-dependent anisotropic Riemannian metric that assigns low transport cost along locally supported tangent directions while penalizing normal velocity components. translated_title: PACE：面向单细胞轨迹推断的几何感知桥接传输方法
translated_abstract: 从破坏性时间序列快照中进行单细胞轨迹推断本质上是一个病态问题：既无法观测到跨时间点的细胞对应关系，也无法观测到连续轨迹，因此仅凭快照分布无法唯一确定潜在的动力学过程。现有的最优传输和基于流的方法通常在观测时钟时间下依据欧氏邻近度来耦合细胞，当发育过程不同步、同一实验时间点采样的细胞处于不同潜在伪时间阶段时，这种方法可能导致轨迹错位。我们提出了PACE，一个从破坏性时间序列快照中恢复几何一致的连续传输动力学的轨迹推断框架，它由三个相互耦合的组件构成。首先，PACE构建了一个依赖于状态和时间的各向异性黎曼度量，该度量在局部支持的切线方向上赋予较低的传输成本，同时惩罚法向速度分量。其次，……
tldr: PACE通过构建状态和时间依赖的各向异性黎曼度量等三个耦合组件，从破坏性单细胞时间序列快照中恢复几何一致的连续传输动力学，解决了发育异步导致的轨迹错位这一核心难题。
en_tdlr: PACE is a geometry-aware bridge transport framework that recovers geometry-consistent continuous transport dynamics from destructive single-cell time-course snapshots, using a state- and time-dependent anisotropic Riemannian metric among three coupled components to resolve trajectory misalignment caused by asynchronous development.
